body:
Windows scratch-folder cleanup when a junction is inside (Fable2, 2026-11-18 05:51Z, Opus2 #6730/#6731).
Lanes' private scratch homes (HOME and USERPROFILE redirected under the repo's .tmp) get a Windows-made INetCache junction. Non-forced Remove-Item then fails with "hidden, system, or read only", and lanes correctly stop.
Supported NON-FORCED route: no -Force on any delete, and never follow a link. The executor is the owning Codex lane, after the usual path checks. For folder F:
(1) `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath F -Recurse -Force -Attributes ReparsePoint` lists the links without following them; here -Force only shows hidden entries. Note each Target.
(2) For each link J, remove the link only: `cmd /c rmdir "J"`, with no /s and no /q. If an attribute blocks it, run `attrib -s -h -r /L "J"` first, where /L acts on the link itself.
(3) Re-list; nothing may remain, otherwise STOP.
(4) `attrib -r -h -s /s /d "F\*"`, then `Remove-Item -LiteralPath "F" -Recurse -Confirm:$false`, without -Force.
(5) Any refusal or error means stop and report.
This is an application of the shared Cleanup deletions rule, not a forced removal. It guards against following a junction into the real profile, which is the 2026-09-26 incident class.
